summary_en: This phase 3 trial compares minimally invasive surgery (MIS) with laparotomy, an open surgery, in people with stage IIIC or IV ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian tube cancer who received chemotherapy before surgery. MIS uses small incisions and is done within 6 weeks after the last cycle of chemotherapy given before surgery, and standard chemotherapy is given again within 6 weeks after surgery. The record does not state a primary outcome; the summary says the study looks at how long before the disease returns and at quality of life after surgery.
summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 3 compara la cirugía mínimamente invasiva (MIS) con la laparotomía, una cirugía abierta, en personas con cáncer de ovario, peritoneo primario o trompa de Falopio en etapa IIIC o IV que recibieron quimioterapia antes de la cirugía. La MIS usa incisiones pequeñas y se realiza dentro de las 6 semanas posteriores al último ciclo de quimioterapia previa a la cirugía, y se administra quimioterapia estándar nuevamente dentro de las 6 semanas posteriores a la cirugía. El registro no indica un resultado principal; el resumen dice que el estudio analiza cuánto tiempo pasa antes de que la enfermedad regrese y la calidad de vida después de la cirugía.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with stage IIIC or IV high-grade ovarian, peritoneal, or fallopian tube cancer.
Considered a surgical candidate after 3 to 4 cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy.
Complete radiologic resolution of disease outside the abdomen; pleural effusion allowed at PI discretion.
CA-125 normalized or at most 500, with a planned diagnostic laparoscopy if applicable.
ECOG performance status 0 to 2, surgery within 6 weeks of last chemotherapy cycle.
not_for: Tumor not suitable for minimally invasive removal on pre-operative imaging.
Ascites not improving during chemotherapy (trace ascites allowed).
Tumor involvement of bowel, colon or rectum, diaphragm, spleen, liver, or mesentery.
Inability to tolerate prolonged Trendelenburg position or pneumoperitoneum.
Psychological, family, social, or geographic barriers to follow-up, or other contraindication to MIS.
